CH+ and Up go to the previous channel

Normally CH+ and D-pad Up go to the next channel and CH− and Down to the previous one. Turn this on to swap them while you watch, in full screen and in the mini player. Browsing lists are not affected.
Type a channel number in the live player

Type a channel number on the remote in the full-screen live player to jump to that channel. Turn this off to leave the number buttons free for your remote shortcuts. Typing a number also needs Channel numbers on in the Live TV settings.

This device runs Android %1$s. Below Android 12 the TV can\'t tell МОЁ ТВ which refresh rates it can switch to smoothly, so changing the rate may black the screen out for a second or two — sometimes more than once during a programme.\n\nWe recommend leaving Auto frame rate off here. If your TV switches cleanly, turn it on and see: you can change it back at any time.

How close to the live broadcast to play. Lower means closer to live but a smaller buffer, so weak streams may stutter or reconnect more. Applies to the next channel you open.

Playing closer to the live broadcast leaves a smaller buffer. On slower connections or unstable streams this can cause more buffering, stutter, or reconnects.\n\nChoose Balanced if a channel becomes unreliable.

Open streams in an external app (VLC, MX Player) instead of the built-in player, chosen per section. Useful for streams this app can\'t decode, or if you prefer another player. Resume position and prev/next are unavailable while playing externally; streams needing a custom User-Agent or referer may not play.

Collect this much video before a live channel starts playing, and again after a stutter. This is an amount of video, not a countdown. Opens МОЁ ТВ each time the TV wakes from sleep, also when you woke it for another app. If App startup opens a channel, every wake-up starts that stream. While this is on, МОЁ ТВ keeps a small background service with a silent notification. Like auto start on boot, it needs permission to display over other apps.
Looks up your provider’s addresses with a DNS server of your choice instead of your network’s own — useful when your network blocks or redirects them.
